status: Prepared for a fresh grounded evaluation against the expanded multi-source corpus. Version 0.4 changes corpus/version metadata only; no v0.4 performance result is included in this file.
purpose: Development evaluation for the English-language Bangladesh criminal-procedure assistant. The 20 gold cases remain CrPC-focused; the active retrieval corpus now also includes the Evidence Act, 1872. This is a starter development set, not a comprehensive or held-out legal benchmark.

source_edition.description: Gold-answer provenance remains the downloaded English Bangladesh Code CrPC archive. The source URL contains 2021-11-23; this is an asset-path date, not a certified amendment cutoff. Runtime retrieval is now multi-source and also includes the Evidence Act, 1872.
excluded_from_substantive_answers: Verified current CrPC amendments absent from the indexed archive
Schedule/form content not indexed for retrieval
The Evidence Act is indexed as a related law, but this evaluation's gold answers remain CrPC-focused
source_edition.scope_note: Gold answers are checked against the cited original CrPC PDF pages, not limited to sample.txt. Runtime retrieval now uses 697 active section/range records: 515 from CrPC Parts 2 and 3 and 182 from the Evidence Act, 1872. The sample hash is retained for CrPC evaluation provenance. CrPC Parts 1 and 4 are validated source documents but are not indexed for retrieval. Historical footnote evidence remains part of the source material; this development set does not treat the expanded corpus as verified current consolidated law.

model_instruction: Answer in English from the specified source edition and supplied evidence. Attribute legal statements to that edition; do not imply it is verified current law. Ask for clarification when essential details are missing. If evidence is insufficient, explain the gap without inventing facts or citations. Include section citations and source excerpts when answering from retrieved text. Provide legal information, not personalized legal advice.
evaluation_rules: Keep the dataset version, source hashes and model instruction fixed when comparing experiments. A source update requires a new dataset version and review of affected expectations.

Record the actual instruction and context for each run. The historical LLM-only baseline uses its general-knowledge prompt; grounded runs use retrieved passages. Different prompts, corpus scopes or dataset versions are not a controlled ablation.
Never provide reference_answer, required_points, must_not_claim, gold source selections or evidence snippets to the model as part of a test prompt.
Accept accurate paraphrases. For answer cases, check every required point, essential qualifiers and absence of forbidden claims; do not use exact-string matching as the correctness metric.
Score answer correctness, expected behavior and citation validity separately. Record failure examples and observed outputs; no model run or performance result is included in this file.

For grounded answer cases, citations must resolve to the expected section and a source page supporting the claim; excerpts must match the cited source. Q08 needs both pages 98 and 99 for its full answer.
For clarification or insufficient-evidence cases, assess the stated gap and avoidance of invented conclusions. An empty sources list is intentional; do not require a fabricated legal citation.
A statement absent from the frozen corpus is unsupported for this evaluation even if true elsewhere. Do not label every unsupported statement factually false.
The revised set concentrates on sections 1, 173 and 174. Expand coverage and add held-out questions before claiming general CrPC performance.

Question prompts must not reveal section numbers, subsection identifiers, statute numbers or evaluation terms such as archive, corpus or prepared sample. Legal references belong in answers and citation metadata.

review.method: Version 0.4 metadata review after expanding the active retrieval corpus from 515 CrPC records to 697 total records by adding 182 Evidence Act records. The 20 prompts, expected behaviors, reference answers, required points, forbidden claims and gold evidence are unchanged from version 0.3.
review.note: The official site was previously consulted for cross-checking and amendment-gap identification. Online text is not injected into evaluation requests. Adding the Evidence Act does not resolve the known missing-current-CrPC-amendment limitations tested by Q18-Q19.

cases.question: What is the main law for criminal court procedures in Bangladesh, and when did it first take effect?
cases.reference_answer: The source calls it the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. Section 1(1) says it came into force on 1 July 1898.
required_points: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
Commencement: 1 July 1898
must_not_claim: 22 March 1898 is the commencement date

evidence: This Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
it shall come into force on the first day of July, 1898

cases.question: Does the same criminal procedure law cover all of Bangladesh? What if a special law provides a different procedure?
cases.reference_answer: It extends to the whole of Bangladesh. In the absence of a specific provision to the contrary, it does not affect a special law in force, a special jurisdiction or power, or a special form of procedure prescribed by another law in force.
required_points: Whole of Bangladesh
Preserves the listed special laws, jurisdictions, powers and procedures
Qualifier: unless a specific provision provides otherwise
must_not_claim: The Code always overrides every special law
Special laws can never be affected under any circumstances

evidence: It extends to the whole of Bangladesh
in the absence of any specific provision to the contrary
or any special jurisdiction or power conferred, or any special form of procedure prescribed, by any other law for the time being in force

cases.question: After an investigation ends, which police officer sends the report, who receives it, and is there a prescribed form?
cases.reference_answer: In the supplied archive, the officer in charge sends the report to a Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence on a police report. The report must use the form prescribed by the Government.
required_points: A Magistrate empowered to take cognizance on a police report
The officer in charge forwards the report
Government-prescribed form
must_not_claim: The report must always be sent directly to the High Court
Any court is an interchangeable recipient

evidence: the officer in charge of the police-station
forward to a Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence on a police-report a report, in the form prescribed by the Government

cases.question: What information should be included in the police report about a criminal case?
cases.reference_answer: The supplied archive requires the report to identify the parties, the nature of the information and people acquainted with the circumstances. For an arrested accused, it must state whether the person was forwarded in custody or released on bond and, if released, whether with or without sureties.
required_points: Names of the parties and nature of the information
Names of people acquainted with the circumstances
Arrested accused's custody or bond status, including sureties
must_not_claim: An invented list of mandatory fields
The report alone proves guilt

evidence: setting forth the names of the parties, the nature of the information and the names of the persons who appear to be acquainted with the circumstances of the case
whether the accused (if arrested) has been forwarded in custody or has been released on his bond
whether with or without sureties

cases.question: I reported an offence to the police. Should they tell me what action they took?
cases.reference_answer: Yes. Section 173(1)(b) requires the officer in charge to communicate the action taken to the person, if any, who first supplied information about the offence, in the prescribed manner.
required_points: Communicate the action taken
Recipient is the person who first supplied the information, if any
In the prescribed manner
must_not_claim: This clause guarantees the informant a free copy of the full report
This clause sets a seven-day notification deadline

evidence: communicate, in such manner as may be prescribed by the Government, the action taken by him to the person, if any, by whom the information relating to the commission of the offence was first given

cases.question: When must a police report go through a senior officer before reaching court, and can that officer ask for more investigation?
cases.reference_answer: In the supplied archive, this route applies where a superior police officer has been appointed under section 158 and a general or special Government order directs submission through that officer. Pending the Magistrate's orders, that officer may direct the officer in charge to investigate further.
required_points: Superior officer appointed under section 158
A general or special Government order directs submission through that officer
May direct further investigation pending the Magistrate's orders
must_not_claim: All police reports automatically require this route
The superior officer decides guilt instead of the Magistrate

evidence: Where a superior officer of police has been appointed under section 158
the report shall in any cases in which the Government by general or special order so directs, be submitted through that officer
make further investigation

cases.question: The police have finished investigating and sent their report to the magistrate. It says I was released on a bond. What happens to that bond now?
cases.reference_answer: If the report shows the accused was released on bond, the supplied provision requires the Magistrate to make an order concerning discharge of the bond, or otherwise as the Magistrate thinks fit. Release on bond does not by itself establish that the case has ended.
required_points: Magistrate makes an order
Discharge of the bond or another order as the Magistrate thinks fit
must_not_claim: The bond is automatically discharged without an order
Release on bond automatically amounts to acquittal

evidence: the Magistrate shall make such order for the discharge of such bond or otherwise as he thinks fit

cases.question: What documents and witness statements should the police send to the court along with their report?
cases.reference_answer: The supplied rule applies to cases covered by section 170. For those cases, the police officer must send the Magistrate the documents or relevant extracts the prosecution proposes to rely on, except those already sent during investigation. The officer must also send the section 161(3) statements of everyone the prosecution proposes to examine as a witness. The indexed archive now includes section 170, but the question gives no case-specific facts establishing whether the user's case qualifies.
required_points: Applies to a case covered by section 170
Documents or relevant extracts relied on by the prosecution
Exception for documents already sent during investigation
Section 161(3) statements of proposed prosecution witnesses
Keep the case-category qualification; do not decide whether the user's case qualifies from the question alone
must_not_claim: The exception covers witness statements as well as documents
Every person's statement is required regardless of whether the prosecution proposes to call them
This attachment requirement applies without qualification to every police report

evidence: When such report is in respect of a case to which section 170 applies
all documents or relevant extracts thereof on which the prosecution proposes to rely other than those already sent to the Magistrate during investigation
the statements recorded under sub-section (3) of section 161 of all the persons whom the prosecution proposes to examine as its witnesses

cases.question: Can the police investigate again after they have already sent their report to court?
cases.reference_answer: The supplied archive permits further investigation after a report has been sent under section 173(1). If further oral or documentary evidence is obtained, the officer in charge must send a further report or reports in the prescribed form. Subsections (1) to (3A) apply as far as may be. This describes the archived provision; later amendments have not been verified.
required_points: Further investigation is not precluded
Further oral or documentary evidence leads to a further report in the prescribed form
Subsections (1)-(3A) apply as far as may be
must_not_claim: Submission permanently bars further investigation
The cited clause expressly requires prior judicial permission
The cited clause establishes an unrestricted right regardless of every other law

evidence: Nothing in this section shall be deemed to preclude further investigation
obtains further evidence, oral or documentary
the provisions of sub-section (1) to (3A) shall, as far as may be, apply

cases.question: I'm accused in a criminal case. Can I get a copy of the police report before the inquiry or trial starts?
cases.reference_answer: Yes. On application, the accused is to receive a copy of a report forwarded under this section before the inquiry or trial begins. Payment is the default, unless the Magistrate considers a free copy appropriate for a special reason.
required_points: Accused must apply
Copy before the inquiry or trial starts
Payment normally required; special-reason exception decided by Magistrate
must_not_claim: Copies can only be supplied after trial
Copies are always free
A specific application form or fee not present in the source

evidence: on application, be furnished to the accused before the commencement of the inquiry or trial
the same shall be paid for unless the Magistrate for some special reason thinks fit to furnish it free of cost

cases.question: I'm the accused, so I'll automatically get the police report for free, right?
cases.reference_answer: No. In the supplied text, the accused receives the copy on application. The copy is normally paid for; the Magistrate may provide it free for a special reason.
required_points: Correct the false premise
Application is required
Paid by default; Magistrate may allow a free copy for a special reason
must_not_claim: The question's free-without-application premise is correct
The Magistrate must always waive payment

evidence: on application, be furnished to the accused
the same shall be paid for unless the Magistrate for some special reason thinks fit to furnish it free of cost

cases.question: Can the police leave an investigation pending for as long as they want?
cases.reference_answer: The supplied archive requires investigations to be completed without unnecessary delay, with the report sent as soon as the investigation is completed. That wording does not authorize arbitrary delay. The prepared sources do not establish a verified current numerical deadline, so the assistant must not invent one or say that no other deadlines exist.
required_points: Investigation must be completed without unnecessary delay
Report follows as soon as the investigation is completed
Current numerical deadlines are not established by the prepared sources
must_not_claim: Police may delay indefinitely without restriction
There is no investigation deadline anywhere in current law
An invented number of days presented as grounded in the prepared sources

evidence: Every investigation under this Chapter shall be completed without unnecessary delay
as soon as it is completed

cases.question: Which law introduced the rules about attaching prosecution documents to a police report and sending another report after further investigation?
cases.reference_answer: Yes. The archive's footnote attributes the insertion of the supporting-document and further-investigation provisions, sections 173(3A) and 173(3B), to section 2 and the Schedule of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978 (Ordinance No. XLIX of 1978). This identifies those insertions; it does not establish that every later amendment has been checked.
required_points: Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978
Ordinance No. XLIX of 1978
Section 2 and Schedule
Attribute the answer to the archive's footnote
must_not_claim: Section 2 of the principal CrPC inserted these subsections
These subsections were first inserted by the 2026 amendment

evidence: Sub-sections (3A) and (3B) were inserted by section 2 and Schedule of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978 (Ordinance No. XLIX of 1978)

cases.question: They said they can arrest me. Is that allowed?
cases.reference_answer: Who do you mean by 'they', and what are the circumstances or alleged offence? I need those details to identify the relevant provision.
required_points: Ask who may make the arrest
Ask for the relevant circumstances or alleged offence
Avoid an unconditional legal conclusion
must_not_claim: Arrest is definitely lawful or unlawful on the information given

cases.question: Can I get a copy of a document from my criminal case?
cases.reference_answer: Which document do you want a copy of, and what is your role in the matter, such as accused or informant?
required_points: Clarify the document
Clarify the person's role before applying a rule
must_not_claim: Assume the user is the accused seeking a section 173 report
Invent a fee or application procedure

cases.question: How much will my lawyer charge to handle my criminal case?
cases.reference_answer: The supplied legal texts do not establish your lawyer's fee. It depends on the particular lawyer and arrangement; an amount cannot be determined from this corpus.
required_points: State that the corpus does not establish the fee
Do not invent an amount
must_not_claim: A fixed fee or range supposedly established by the cited CrPC provisions

cases.question: Has the police report been filed in my case, G.R. 123/2026 in Dhaka?
cases.reference_answer: I cannot determine the filing status from statutory PDFs. That requires the actual case record or an authorized case-status source, which this corpus does not contain.
required_points: No access to case-specific filing status
Identify need for the actual case record or an authorized status source
must_not_claim: The report has or has not been filed
Access to a court or police database that the system does not have
cases.note: Synthetic case identifier used only for testing; no real case is asserted.

cases.question: My case is before a first-class magistrate. What is the largest fine that court can impose in 2026?
cases.reference_answer: The current maximum cannot be verified from this archive and its incomplete amendment coverage. The applicable current consolidated provision or amendments must be included before giving a figure for 2026.
required_points: Distinguish the archived edition from the requested current date
State that current amendment coverage is insufficient
Do not give an unverified current limit
must_not_claim: The archive's ten thousand taka is verified as the current limit
An invented replacement limit

cases.question: Under the latest rules, how many days can the police take to finish investigating a criminal case?
cases.reference_answer: The prepared archive does not establish a verified deadline under the latest rules. It contains older wording about avoiding unnecessary delay, but the later investigation-deadline provision, section 173B, is absent from the prepared set. A current official provision must be added before giving a number of days.
required_points: Distinguish the older general duty from a verified current numerical deadline
Explain the missing amendment evidence
Do not mistake missing corpus evidence for absence of a legal deadline
must_not_claim: Current law has no deadline or police have unlimited time
Section 173B does not exist
A numerical deadline presented as supported by the prepared corpus

cases.question: When police receive a report of a suspected unlawful killing, which magistrate should they notify and how soon?
cases.reference_answer: In the archived provision, the officer in charge or another specially empowered police officer must immediately notify the nearest Executive Magistrate empowered to hold inquests. This identifies the notification duty, not the whole investigation procedure or verified current law.
required_points: Nearest Executive Magistrate empowered to hold inquests
Notification must be immediate
must_not_claim: Notify any magistrate interchangeably
Wait for the investigation or trial to finish before notification
The archive establishes verified current law

evidence: shall immediately give intimation thereof to the
Executive Magistrate
empowered to hold inquests
